title: Hierarchical policy merge race causes 'unbounded' inheritance and bypass of route throttle
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
Summary: We observed a production incident where traffic for a small number of orgs briefly bypassed per-route throttles and consumed quota far above configured limits. The root cause appears to be a race in the hierarchical policy merge logic combined with how we represent 'unbounded' policies. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigation, and the longer-term fix plan.

What happened: At ~2026-03-01T09:37:12Z a sudden spike of requests from 3 customers generated an unusual surge of per-key throughput (10-20x expected). The runtime's enforcement logs show the route-level enforcer returning ALLOW for many requests that should have been RATE_LIMITED given org and route quotas. Billing dashboards showed corresponding token usage jumps and some customers received quota-exceeded alerts after the fact.

Scope: Affected path is the policy merge and evaluate flow (policy-loader -> policy-merge -> effective-policy cache -> route-enforcer). Only services using hierarchical policies (org -> project -> route) with at least one policy explicitly set to 'unbounded' were impacted. Rough estimate: 0.08% of traffic across hosted cluster during window; customer-facing high-severity for 3 orgs.

Reproduction steps (dev/staging):
1) Create org-level policy with per-minute limit = 1000
2) Create project-level policy with per-minute limit = 500 and route-level policy marked 'unbounded' (sentinel = null or MAX)
3) Deploy a policy-loader refresh during high-concurrency request generation (use loadgen with 1k concurrent connections)
4) Observe route-enforcer allowing >500 req/min while metric delta shows project limit not applied

Observed logs and artifacts:
- Enforcer trace snippets: 'merge_policies: selected_limit=MAX_INT effective_window=60s' followed by 'evaluate: allow for key=org:123 route=/v1/chat'
- policy-loader audit: 'hot-reload: applied delta for org:123 at 2026-03-01T09:37:11.985Z'
- Dashboard: /dashboards/billing/spikes?window=2026-03-01T09:30..09:45 (internal)
- Incident runbook notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/2026-03-01-rate-merge-bypass
- Draft PR with additional logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123

Hypothesis / root cause:
1) Policy representation: we encode 'unbounded' as a sentinel numeric MAX (2^63-1) to simplify arithmetic in evaluation.
2) Merge algorithm picks the most permissive candidate by numeric comparison during hierarchical merges (org vs project vs route).
3) During concurrent policy refresh, a transient state existed where the project-level policy record was briefly omitted from the in-memory policy set (race between delete+add operations from the loader).
4) When merging, route-level 'unbounded' with sentinel MAX compared greater than project-level finite limit, so the resulting effective policy for the key ended up MAX.
5) Combined with short TTL on effective-policy cache and the timing of refresh, requests in that window used the wrong merged policy, resulting in bypass.

Why this is different from previous 'shard/failover' bugs: the failure is logical (merge ordering + sentinel semantics) not a storage replication gap. Existing tickets focus on shard rebalances and duplicate credits; this is an invariance violation in the merge comparator and sentinel design.

Mitigations applied:
- Short-term hotfix (deployed 2026-03-01 10:05Z): change merge comparator to prefer the most restrictive non-unbounded value if any non-unbounded exists in the ancestor chain (fallback rule). This was deployed as enforcer-2.4.1-hotfix.
- Killswitch: added runtime flag 'enforce-prefer-restrictive-merge' to protect older clusters while we roll out.

Proposed long-term fixes:
1) Policy model change: represent 'unbounded' with explicit enum rather than numeric sentinel; require merge to understand unbounded semantics (explicit precedence rules).
2) Atomic policy refresh: coalesce loader updates for a single org/project into a single atomic swap to prevent intermediate omission states.
3) Add unit + fuzz tests around merge semantics: combinations of bounded/unbounded values across 3 levels and concurrent update sequences.
4) Backfill audit traces: emit 'effective-policy-source' in enforcer logs so we can trace where the effective limit originated (org/project/route) for any allow/deny decision.

Acceptance criteria (done when):
- Merge implementation uses explicit unbounded type and deterministic precedence documented in code and Confluence.
- Loader performs atomic swap for policy bundles; tests ensure no intermediate missing-project state observable by enforcer.
- New unit+integration tests added and passing in CI.
- Rollout plan executed to all clusters and monitoring shows no similar spike for 7 days.

Implementation plan and timeline:
- 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-06: implement model change and merge logic (+ unit tests) (owner: Aisha)
- 2026-03-07 to 2026-03-09: implement atomic bundle loader and integration tests (owner: Dev infra)
- 2026-03-10: internal canary on staging and a single-hosted region (owner: SRE)
- 2026-03-11 to 2026-03-13: progressive rollout across regions with runtime flag enabled by default after canary (owner: SRE/infra)
- 2026-03-14: disable hotfix fallback and monitor for regressions (rollback window 2 hours)

Testing notes:
- Added a concurrency fuzz harness that simulates concurrent loader updates while loadgen exercises enforcers.
- Integration test covers 1k concurrent clients and asserts no effective-policy ever becomes 'MAX_INT' when any ancestor level is bounded.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Backwards compatibility: changing policy model requires conversion for persisted bundles; we plan a migration path in loader that reads old numeric sentinels and writes explicit type. This is slightly more complex but safer than keeping sentinel arithmetic.
- Performance: explicit enum handling adds a branch in hot path evaluation. Measurement in benchmark shows ~0.6% p99 latency increase in synthetic microbench; we'll micro-optimize if needed (e.g., precompute bitmask).

Review feedback so far:
- PM (Dana Liu): prioritize auditability; requester asked for 'effective-policy-source' field in logs — added.
- Security (Noah Kim): no secrets or data exposure; ok.
- SRE (Miguel Ortega): require a killswitch and staged rollout — implemented.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/2026-03-01-rate-merge-bypass
- Draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RATE/Explicit-Unbounded-Policy-Design
- Draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/enforcer/pull/877 (merge logic), https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4155 (atomic loader)
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/policy-merge-canary

Next steps: finish implementation tasks assigned to Aisha and infra, land PRs, run canary, then full rollout. After rollout, schedule a 1-week observation window and postmortem update with final root-cause and learnings.
